title: Equal Material Huh?
reviewNotes: Four branches, 18 exact positions from complete six-piece board. Bd3 prepares Bg6 against ...Qh5+, Qb2+ lures ...Bf6, and Qb5 creates two mating routes. Source ...Qe1 permits Qh5 mate; ...Bd8 permits Qe8 mate. Accepting Bd3 leads to Qg7 mate. Immediate Qb8+ ...Qd8 draws.
transcript: Equal material does not mean unequal position. In this situation, both sides have a queen and a bishop, but white is completely winning thanks to a pretty incredible sequence. First of all, you cannot just go for a checkmate like this because black is going to block the check. And then if you go to this file, now the bishop is going to block the check. And if you try to go to the diagonal, black is actually going to sacrifice the bishop like this. And now with only a bishop left, there is no way to checkmate. So, white has to become creative and find the only move. Bishop to D3, a brilliant sacrifice that relies on the fact that the queen cannot take this bishop or otherwise queen to B2 is going to lead to a checkmate in just two moves. And luckily, all of these queen checks are somehow covered by the white pieces. But black does have one more check. Queen to H5. Now, of course, the king doesn't want to move away and allow breathing space for this black king. So, we play bishop to G6, counter-attacking the queen. But it seems like black is simply out of the woods. After queen to H4, you still cannot give a check here. The bishop is just going to cover and you have no checks on this file. But surprisingly, white still has queen to B2 check. What? This doesn't make any sense. The bishop can cover and now we still cannot take it because with a bishop left, we cannot win. And that is true, but whoever said that we wanted to take this bishop, we just wanted to lure it in front of the king so that now we could play queen to B5. The queen is trying to infiltrate from three different positions. And incredibly, there are no checks only thanks to the bishop on F6. Otherwise, the black queen would be able to just give perpetual checks and save a draw. But from here, there's nothing to do. If black tries to save this check, there's going to be queen to H5 checkmate. And if he tries to cover from here, there's going to be queen to E8 checkmate. Follow for more incredible chess.
